title: Horizontal filtration of the cone of a first-quadrant total map
statement: Let $C$ be abelian [def-sp-abelian] with totals for all first-quadrant bicomplexes [def-sp-double-complex-total], and let $f:A\to B$ be a morphism of first-quadrant bicomplexes. Extend total complexes by zero to integer degrees and set $M=\operatorname{Cone}(\operatorname{Tot}(f))$. There is a decreasing subcomplex filtration $F$ [def-sp-filtration] of $M$. Its degreewise steps [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients] satisfy $F^0M^n=M^n$ and $F^{n+2}M^n=0$ for every integer $n$. For every $p<0$, $H^n(\operatorname{gr}^p_FM)=0$ in every degree. For every $p\ge0$ and integer $n$, there is an isomorphism $H^n(\operatorname{gr}^p_FM)\cong H^{n-p}(\operatorname{Cone}(\operatorname{extend}(f^{p,\bullet})))$. No quasi-isomorphism hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: First horizontal filtration and its graded complexes; column-cone refinement of the finite endpoint comparison argument.

proof.text: Construct the finite horizontal tails S_{p,n}. Their stability under the cone differential is coneHorizontal_step_stable. Restrict d uniquely through the monic step inclusions; square zero follows after composing with those monomorphisms. The inclusions of finite indexing sets give antitone subcomplex maps. Taking their subobject classes produces F with complexStep(p,n)=S_{p,n}. This assembly is proved in Lean by filtration_of_degreewise.

source.place: First horizontal filtration, displayed formula preceding Lemma 12.25.1; columnwise mapping-cone refinement of parent node proof steps 1 and 3.

proof.text: At p=0 all source and target cone summands occur. Their maps jointly detect morphisms from the cone, by total.hom_ext on the nonnegative extended totals and mappingCone.ext_from; in negative total degrees extension is zero. Thus S_{0,n}=top. At p=n+2 the indexing set is empty, so S_{n+2,n}=bottom. These are coneHorizontalStep_zero and coneHorizontalStep_finite.

source.place: First horizontal filtration, displayed formula preceding Lemma 12.25.1; columnwise mapping-cone refinement of parent node proof steps 1 and 3.

proof.text: For p<=0 the filter condition on natural horizontal indices is automatic, so S_{p,n}=top. A subcomplex whose inclusion has full image in every degree is the whole complex, because each component is a monic isomorphism. Hence for p<0 both F.step(p) and F.step(p+1) are top. Their inclusion is an isomorphism and its cokernel is zero; applying the homology functor proves the negative-filtration vanishing.

proof.text: For p>=0 obtain the chain isomorphism from coneHorizontal_graded_iso. Apply the homology functor and compose with CochainComplex.ShiftSequence.shiftIso for the shift -p. The equation -p+n=n-p gives the required homology degree.

lean.statement: theorem firstQuadrant_vertical_cone_filtration {A B : HomologicalComplex₂ C (ComplexShape.up ℕ) (ComplexShape.up ℕ)} (f : A ⟶ B) : ∃ F : DecreasingFiltration (CochainComplex.mappingCone (HomologicalComplex.extendMap (total.map f (ComplexShape.up ℕ)) ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat)), (∀ n : ℤ, F.complexStep 0 n = ⊤ ∧ F.complexStep (n + 2) n = ⊥) ∧ (∀ p n : ℤ, p < 0 → IsZero ((F.gradedPiece p).homology n)) ∧ (∀ p n : ℤ, 0 ≤ p → Nonempty ((F.gradedPiece p).homology n ≅ (CochainComplex.mappingCone (HomologicalComplex.extendMap (f.f p.toNat) ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat)).homology (n - p)))
